assistant|route_option_1: Assistant suggested the Grand Teton and Yellowstone Loop: I-90 to Jackson, Wyoming, Grand Teton NP, Yellowstone NP, Beartooth Highway to Montana, then back via I-90
assistant|route_option_2: Assistant suggested Utah's Mighty Five: I-70 to Moab, then Arches, Canyonlands, Capitol Reef, Bryce Canyon, and Zion National Parks
assistant|route_option_3: Assistant suggested California's Sierra Nevada route: I-80 to Sacramento, then Yosemite, Sequoia, and Kings Canyon National Parks
assistant|beartooth_highway_details: Beartooth Highway (US-212) is a 68-mile scenic road connecting Cooke City, Montana to Red Lodge, Montana through the Beartooth Mountains
assistant|beartooth_summer_conditions: In summer the Beartooth Highway is fully paved, two lanes with passing lanes, speed limit 45-65 mph, mild weather with occasional thunderstorms
assistant|beartooth_altitude: The Beartooth Highway reaches elevations over 10,000 feet, which can cause altitude sickness
assistant|campground_recommendation: Assistant recommended Colter Bay Campground: 350 sites on Jackson Lake, RVs/trailers up to 45 feet, flush toilets, showers, potable water
Assistant recommended Jenny Lake Campground: 49 sites near Moose, RVs/trailers up to 30 feet, flush toilets, showers, potable water
Assistant recommended Signal Mountain Campground: 235 sites on Jackson Lake, RVs/trailers up to 30 feet, flush toilets, showers, potable water
Assistant recommended Granite Creek Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest: 61 sites, RVs up to 40 feet, flush toilets, showers
Assistant recommended Curtis Canyon Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest: 12 sites, RVs up to 30 feet, vault toilets, potable water
Assistant recommended Jackson Hole Campground at Fireside Resort in Wilson, Wyoming: 200 sites for all-size RVs, flush toilets, showers, pool, Wi-Fi
Assistant recommended Virginian Lodge RV Resort in Jackson, Wyoming: 230 sites for all-size RVs, flush toilets, showers, pool, hot tub, Wi-Fi
assistant|colter_bay_electric_hookups: Colter Bay Campground has 100 of 350 campsites with 30-amp electric hookups in the 'Electric Loop' section, for RVs up to 45 feet
assistant|colter_bay_reservation_process: Electric sites at Colter Bay are reserved via recreation.gov by selecting 'Electric' site type; 6-month reservation window
assistant|colter_bay_potable_water: Colter Bay Campground has several potable water stations near the entrance, dump station, and throughout; water pressure can be high so use a regulator
assistant|colter_bay_dump_station: Colter Bay Campground's dump station is near the entrance, free for campers with donations appreciated, for RV waste only
assistant|colter_bay_water_rules: Colter Bay's potable water is not for washing vehicles; campground is in a water-sensitive area so conserve water
assistant|yellowstone_summer_crowds: Summer is peak tourist season in Yellowstone and Grand Teton, so expect crowds and long lines; book accommodations in advance
assistant|bear_safety_advice: Both Yellowstone and Grand Teton have bears, so carry bear spray and know how to use it
